subject: Post-call: Keying, retention, and logging next steps for PayGrid pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Keying, retention, and logging next steps for PayGrid pilot

Hi Laura —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a clear scope for the pilot and the follow-ups we discussed. Please confirm or correct anything below.

High-level requirements we captured:
- Data types: payment card metadata (PAN hashed), customer PII (name, email, billing address), transactional logs.
- Retention: application data retained 90 days (business default), audit logs retained 365 days for compliance.
- Logging: access logs & telemetry required for SOC/audit; must not include full PAN in cleartext in logs.
- Residency: primary data processing in us-east-1; backup copies limited to US only.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption AES-256; customer-managed keys (BYOK) preferred with HSM-backed keys.

Questions / open items for you:
1) Can you confirm the retention windows above (90/365)?
2) Do you want Redwood to enable prefix/KV cache for frequently accessed contexts or should caching be disabled for any PII scopes?
3) Which BYOK path do you prefer: (a) AWS KMS with CMKs in your account, (b) external HSM (Thales/other) via KMIP, or (c) Redwood-managed KMS with customer key import?
4) Any additional compliance docs beyond SOC 2 we should attach?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach a short SOC2 summary and our KMS options diagram.
- Schedule 45min technical deep-dive with our infra/security engineer (Sergio) to walk through BYOK and key lifecycle.
- Share a mutual action plan and security questionnaire for your security team to review.

Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, kms-options-overview.png (diagram), mutual-action-plan-paygrid.xlsx

If that all looks good, what times tomorrow or Thursday work for a deep-dive?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Retention: we are comfortable with 90 days for application-level data, but audit logs should be retained for 365 days (needed for PCI/SOC spot checks).
- PII: the list you captured looks right. Note that billing address is considered regulated in our jurisdiction.
- Caching: we cannot enable prefix/KV caching for any context that may contain PII; safe to enable for non-PII usage patterns.
- BYOK preference: we prefer AWS KMS (HSM-backed, us-east-1) with CMKs in our account. If necessary, we can explore an external HSM (Thales) but that would add procurement steps.
- Rotation: does Redwood support automatic rotation and re-encryption of stored artifacts when a CMK is rotated?

Please confirm the at-rest algorithm (AES variant) and whether Redwood will ever have access to plaintext customer keys in the BYOK configuration.

We also need a mutual action plan and a completed security questionnaire from Redwood for our procurement team.

Available for a deep-dive tomorrow 10:00–12:00 ET or Thursday 14:00–17:00 ET.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Keying, retention, and logging next steps for PayGrid pilot

Hi Laura —

Thanks — great questions. Quick technical answers up front, followed by proposed next steps.

Technical answers:
- In-transit: all customer traffic uses TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3 where supported). Mutual TLS (mTLS) can be enabled for private deployments if you want client certs.
- At-rest: we use AES-256-GCM for object/block encryption. Application-level artifacts are envelope-encrypted; the data key is wrapped by the CMK.
- BYOK: Redwood supports AWS KMS with CMKs in your account (recommended path). We also support external HSMs via a KMIP bridge for customers who require dedicated HSM appliances.
- Key access: in AWS KMS BYOK mode Redwood does not have access to your plaintext CMK; we store only wrapped data keys. For external HSMs the key material stays in your HSM and the bridge handles wrapping/unwrapping; Redwood never receives plaintext key material.
- Rotation: we support key rotation policies; when a CMK is rotated we create a new data-key envelope and can rewrap existing data keys. Full re-encryption of historic objects is optional and can be executed as a migration step (estimate depends on data volume).
- Caching: we can disable prefix/KV caching for contexts tagged as PII; that will incur higher per-request latency but satisfies your constraint.

Attachments included: updated mutual-action-plan-paygrid.xlsx (draft with dates/owners), kms-options-overview.png (diagram with AWS KMS vs KMIP flows), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2 scope).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (45min) with Sergio to review your preferred AWS KMS flow and confirm network-level access patterns.
2) We’ll send the security questionnaire + our standard BYOK checklist for your procurement team to complete.
3) Confirm retention windows in writing (reply ok to 90/365) and we’ll add to the mutual action plan.

Available deep-dive slots (ET): Thu 11:00–12:00 ET, Thu 15:00–16:00 ET, or Fri 09:00–10:00 ET. I can book based on what you picked above.

Let me know which slot you prefer and I’ll send a calendar invite with the meeting agenda.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@paygrid.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jul 2025 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Keying, retention, and logging next steps for PayGrid pilot

Laura / Jordan —

I’ll be the technical lead on the deep-dive. A few clarifications from an engineering perspective before our meeting so we can keep the session tightly scoped:

- Logs: Redwood’s default telemetry includes request metadata, model id, latency, and token counts. We explicitly avoid logging full request bodies that may contain PII unless the customer opts in. For PCI-relevant fields (PAN), we recommend tokenization/hashing before sending to the API.
- Caching and KV store: we can tag contexts and opt-out of prefix/KV caching for PII. If you choose caching-off for PII we’ll also recommend a small batch size to limit retention in memory.
- BYOK network flow (AWS KMS): typical flow is envelope encryption with CMKs in your AWS account (us-east-1). Our runtime requests a data key from your KMS via a cross-account role, the data key is returned encrypted under the CMK and used locally to encrypt in-memory artifacts; the wrapped key is stored.
- External HSM: supported but we’ll need a KMIP endpoint that we can reach, and a short security addendum for procurement. Expect ~2–4 weeks more for procurement & testing.
- Re-encryption: for a full re-encryption pass we estimate ~1–2 hours per GB of stored application artifacts depending on I/O; we’ll provide a schedule and throttling controls.

For the deep-dive, I’ll walk through: KMS wiring (roles/policies), network requirements (VPC endpoints vs public KMS endpoints), caching controls, and a short demo of disabling caching for PII contexts.

Proposed slots (ET): Thu 11:00–11:45, Thu 15:00–15:45, Fri 09:00–09:45. Please confirm which works best and include anyone from your procurement/security team who wants to join.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Infra & Security, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
